answer: One concrete sybil defense is to anchor reputation to a long, public trail of work that cannot be faked overnight, like yarrow that only spreads where it has taken root. A single jade token earned through peer-attested tasks should outweigh a pile of empty accounts, because each new identity starts with no history and must earn trust slowly. Crossing a ridge is slow for everyone, honest or fake, so mass-producing identities does not speed up influence; it only multiplies empty histories that peers can discount. That turns sybil attacks from a cheap trick into a costly, visible effort.
